issues.display_title: Issue #1830: Integrate Countly analytics SDK (production only)
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

The admin app has no product analytics. We cannot answer basic questions: how many people open the editor, how long a session lasts, where users drop off before publishing, or how often the 3D editor throws runtime errors in the field.

Integrate the Countly Web SDK against our self-hosted server, enabled in production only.

In scope

  • Add countly-sdk-web and initialize it from a browser-only app initializer, so SSR never touches the SDK.
  • Environment config: countlyEnabled, countlyUrl, countlyAppKey in all four environment files.
  • Automatic tracking: sessions, pageviews, unhandled JS errors, click heatmap.
  • Pageviews reported as the route config path (/editor/:id), not the resolved URL, so exhibition ids do not explode the Views table into one row per gallery.
  • Identity: merge the pre-login anonymous device id into the account on login (change_id(id, true)), send profile fields via user_details, and reset to a fresh anonymous id on logout so the next visitor on the same browser is not attributed to the previous account.
  • Editor telemetry: emit an editor_action event with { action, exhibition_id } from EditorService.updateLogActivity(), the single sink that ~90 editor call sites already funnel through (publish, save, rename, upload, align, undo/redo, preview mode, transform updates).
  • Export a trackEvent() helper that no-ops on the server and when Countly is disabled, so call sites need no guards of their own.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not add analytics calls to individual editor call sites; hook the existing sink only.
  • Do not enable Countly outside production. Local, dev, and QA ship with countlyEnabled: false and must issue zero network requests.
  • Do not track per-frame or drag-move events; only discrete user actions (pointer-up and explicit commands).
  • No consent/GDPR gating, custom business funnels, feedback widgets, remote config, or A/B testing in this pass.

Acceptance criteria

  • Production build reports sessions, pageviews, errors, and clicks to the configured Countly server.
  • Views table shows /editor/:id as a single aggregated row, not one row per exhibition id.
  • Logging in attaches the prior anonymous session to the account; logging out returns the browser to a fresh anonymous id.
  • Editor actions appear as editor_action events segmented by action and exhibition id.
  • With countlyEnabled: false, no Countly requests are sent and no SDK errors are thrown, including during SSR.

Verification

  • ng build --configuration production and ng build --configuration development succeed.
  • Editor unit tests show no new failures against the pre-change baseline.
  • SSR: the SDK module loads under Node without touching window, and trackEvent() is inert on the server.
  • Manually confirm in the Countly dashboard: session count, /editor/:id view row, an editor_action event, and a user profile after login.

issues.display_title: Issue #1807: [Style System] Separate Geist UI fonts from Editor content fonts
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Separate product UI typography assets from the Editor user-content font catalogue so Geist adoption cannot alter authored gallery content.

In scope

  • Create distinct UI and Editor-content font registration ownership.
  • Register Geist and Geist Mono for product UI tokens.
  • Preserve every Editor font-family asset URL, mapping, weight, style, preview, and rendered-content rule.
  • Define an explicit boundary preventing body, Editor wrappers, dialogs, and shared controls from forcing Geist onto user-authored content.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not remove, rename, consolidate, or restyle catalogue fonts.
  • Do not migrate all feature typography in this issue.
  • No intended change to current content rendering.

Acceptance criteria

  • UI and content registrations can evolve independently.
  • Automated searches/guardrails protect content-font mappings.
  • Representative catalogue fonts render with the same weights/styles before and after the split.

Dependencies and order

Depends on global import ordering and token foundations. Must precede Editor Geist migration.

Verification

  • Compare Editor content previews and rendered gallery content using at least two different font metrics.
  • Run pnpm test:styles and the required Angular build.
  • Confirm product UI font changes do not cascade into authored content.

issues.display_title: Issue #1808: [Style System] Replace Bootstrap behavior for Editor buttons and fields
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Give Editor controls complete app-owned base and state behavior so the pilot no longer relies on Bootstrap button/form implementations.

In scope

  • Implement the observable display, alignment, border, sizing, focus, active, disabled, loading, and validation behavior used by Editor buttons and fields.
  • Retain useful APIs such as .btn and .form-control where renaming templates adds no value.
  • Replace Bootstrap button mixin usage in the Editor with direct, token-backed CSS.
  • Scope feature-only variants to their owners.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not remove global Bootstrap yet; unmigrated features may still require it.
  • Do not force all controls to one height or redesign states.
  • Preserve Editor user-content typography.

Acceptance criteria

  • Editor buttons and fields render and behave correctly even when Bootstrap rules are excluded from the pilot test context.
  • Keyboard focus, disabled, loading, error, and validation states remain accessible and visually compatible.
  • No new Bootstrap mixin dependency is introduced.

Dependencies and order

Depends on the baseline, token foundations, and font-domain separation. This begins Editor Phase 2A.

Verification

  • Exercise hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, and validation states.
  • Run focused component tests, pnpm test:styles, and the required Angular build.
  • Compare Editor desktop/mobile screenshots.

issues.display_title: Issue #1809: [Style System] Remove Editor tabs and utilities dependency on Bootstrap
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Make the Editor's tab and layout behavior app-owned so Bootstrap utilities are no longer needed in the pilot.

In scope

  • Move Editor and Edit Frame nav-tab behavior to their owning component styles.
  • Replace active Bootstrap grid, display, flex, spacing, and alignment utilities in Editor templates with component layout or a narrowly defined shared helper that has multiple consumers.
  • Document any temporary compatibility selector and its deletion condition.
  • Preserve responsive and overflow behavior at current breakpoints.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not remove Bootstrap globally in this issue.
  • Do not recreate Bootstrap's utility generator or rename unrelated feature-owned classes.
  • No visual redesign or typography migration.

Acceptance criteria

  • Editor tabs and layouts do not require Bootstrap CSS to render or interact correctly.
  • No unexplained Bootstrap utility consumer remains within the Editor pilot scope.
  • Shared helpers are minimal, documented, and backed by real reuse.

Dependencies and order

Depends on app-owned Editor buttons/fields. Complete before Editor ownership cleanup.

Verification

  • Search Editor templates/SCSS for active Bootstrap tab and utility APIs.
  • Test tab selection, overflow, desktop/mobile layout, and keyboard focus.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the required Angular build.
  • Compare baseline screenshots.
